Definition: from the base of G2476; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy:--dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.
BiblicalUsage: The word is a standing against, and in Acts it is always sedition. Paul is charged as a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, Barabbas lay bound for a certain sedition made in the city and for murder, and the insurrection he made is named again at his release.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the charge shows how the world reads the gospel: Paul was called a pestilent fellow for preaching Christ, and the real rebel walked free.
